q: Which AWS service gives access to foundation models from Amazon and other AI companies through a single API, without managing infrastructure?
e: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed, serverless service offering FMs from several providers behind one API.

q: A team wants to run a custom fine-tuned model on Amazon Bedrock. Which purchasing option does this typically require?
e: Custom (fine-tuned) models on Bedrock run with Provisioned Throughput: dedicated model capacity you reserve.

q: A company needs to process 100,000 documents through a Bedrock model overnight, with no need for instant answers. What is the most cost-effective option?
o: Real-time calls one at a time during peak hours
e: Batch inference processes large sets of prompts asynchronously at a lower price than on-demand calls.
an: RPGACE's Fallback Scout queue works this way: prompts wait in a table and get answered later in one go.

q: Which AWS service offers a hub of pre-trained and foundation models that can be deployed and fine-tuned inside SageMaker?
e: SageMaker JumpStart provides ready-made models (including FMs) and solution templates.

q: Which tool lets anyone experiment with building small generative AI apps on Amazon Bedrock with no code?
e: PartyRock is a no-code playground for learning to build generative AI apps on Bedrock.

q: Which AWS service is a generative AI assistant that answers questions using a company's own enterprise data and connected systems?
e: Amazon Q Business connects to company data sources and answers employee questions, respecting their existing access permissions.

q: Which AWS offering helps developers write, explain, debug and transform code with generative AI?
e: Amazon Q Developer (formerly CodeWhisperer) is the AI assistant for software development.

q: What is an AI agent?
o: A system where a model plans steps, uses tools and memory, and takes actions towards a goal
A firewall rule for model endpoints
e: Agents go beyond one answer: they reason, call tools or APIs, keep state and act. That needs guardrails and permissions.
an: Claude Code working on RPGACE is an agent: it plans, runs tools (git, Supabase), keeps notes and acts, with you approving risky steps.

q: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
o: An open standard for connecting AI models to tools and data sources in a consistent way
A type of neural network layer
e: MCP standardises how models discover and call external tools and data, so one integration works across clients.
an: RPGACE's Claude Code sessions reach Supabase and Vercel through MCP connectors: one standard plug for each service.

q: In a multi-agent system, what does an orchestrator agent typically do?
o: Breaks a goal into tasks, sends them to specialised agents and combines the results
e: Orchestration coordinates specialised agents, their order and the hand-offs between them.
an: RPGACE's Claude Code acts as orchestrator for the OpenMontage session, handing work over through the openmontage_jobs queue.

q: Which AWS service provides managed runtime, memory, identity, gateway and observability for deploying AI agents securely at scale?
e: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the set of building blocks for running agents in production, with any framework or model.

q: Which open-source SDK from AWS helps developers build AI agents with a model-driven approach in a few lines of code?
e: Strands Agents is AWS's open-source agent SDK. Agents built with it can be deployed on AgentCore.

q: Which AWS tool is an agentic IDE that turns prompts into specs, then code, for spec-driven development?
e: Kiro is AWS's agentic development environment built around specs, steering and automated hooks.

q: Which describes agent memory in agentic AI?
o: Keeping relevant information from earlier steps or sessions so the agent can use it later
The amount of RAM on the GPU
The size of the training dataset
A backup of the model weights
e: Short-term memory holds the current task's context. Long-term memory persists facts across sessions.
an: RPGACE's session_memory table is long-term memory for Claude Code sessions: each session writes what it decided, and the next one reads it.

q: Why do AI agents need stricter controls than a simple chatbot?
o: Because they can take actions such as calling APIs or changing data
Because they cannot use foundation models
e: Agents act on systems, so they need least-privilege permissions, guardrails, logging and human approval for risky steps.
an: Oracle Control asks you to confirm before it logs a beat or drafts an email. The AI proposes, and you approve the action.

q: Which is a business benefit of generative AI?
o: Faster content creation and higher productivity
No need for any data governance
Lower electricity use than all other software
e: Benefits include speed, productivity, personalisation, adaptability and simpler interfaces, with risks to manage.

q: Which metric best measures the business value of a generative AI customer service assistant?
o: Reduction in average handling time and improved customer satisfaction
e: Business metrics (efficiency, conversion, satisfaction, cost per interaction) show value. Technical settings don't.

q: Which term describes the cost of a generative AI app growing as more tokens are processed?
e: With token-based pricing, cost scales with prompt and output length times the number of calls.
an: RPGACE's token-cost audit (after £10 went in one test session) led to rules: short prompts, cheap filters before any AI call, no extra 'triage' calls.

q: What is prompt caching?
o: Reusing the processed part of a repeated prompt prefix to cut cost and latency
Saving every answer to a database
e: When many requests share the same long prefix (instructions, documents), caching it avoids reprocessing and lowers cost.
an: RPGACE turned on prompt caching for Oracle's long, repeated instructions.

q: Which describes model distillation?
o: Training a smaller student model to copy a larger teacher model's behaviour
Splitting data into train and test sets
e: Distillation produces a smaller, faster, cheaper model that keeps much of the larger model's quality for a target task. Bedrock supports it.

q: A startup has little ML expertise and wants to add text generation to its app this week. What is the best starting point?
o: Call a foundation model through Amazon Bedrock
Build a GPU cluster and pre-train a model
Hire a team to label a billion documents
e: Managed FM APIs give the fastest path, with no infrastructure or ML training required.

q: Which statement about how Amazon Bedrock handles customer data is correct?
o: Prompts and outputs are not used to train the underlying base models
All prompts are shared with every model provider for training
Data is always stored in a single global Region
Bedrock requires you to upload data publicly
e: Bedrock doesn't use your inputs or outputs to train base models. Data stays in your chosen Region and is encrypted.

q: Which describes context engineering?
o: Choosing and arranging exactly what information goes into a model's limited context window
e: Context engineering curates instructions, retrieved data, memory and tool results so the model has what it needs, without clutter or waste.
an: Oracle's grounding only adds live app facts when your question needs them (a keyword gate), instead of stuffing everything in every time.

q: Generative AI answers can become out of date. What is the main reason?
o: Models only know what was in their training data up to a cut-off date
e: A model's knowledge stops at its training cut-off. RAG or tools can add current information.
